title: Draft: epan: Register static column fields and make them filterable
description:
Make the text of each column a FT_STRING field that can be filtered,
prefixed with _ws.col - these work in display filters, filters in taps,
coloring rules, Wireshark read filters, and in the -Y, -R, and -e options
to tshark. Use them as the default "Apply as Filter" value for the columns
that aren't handled by anything else currently.

Use the lower case version of the rest of the COL_* define for each
column as the field name.

Note that only column formats that actually correspond to columns get
filled in (invisible columns work).

This adds a number of conditions to "when are the columns needed",
including when the main display filter or any filter on a tap is
using one of these fields. For custom columns, the tree then has
to be further primed with any fields used by the custom columns as well.

Thus for custom columns, or for a number of built-in columns, you're
better off for performance reasons matching the ordinary field; it
takes extra time to generate the columns and many of them are numeric
types. (Note that you can always convert a non-string field to a string
field if you want regex matching, consult the *wireshark-filter(4)* man
page.) It does save a bit on typing (especially for a multifield custom
column) and remembering the column title might be easier in some cases.

The columns are set before the color filters, which means that you
can have a color filter that depends on a built-in column like Info or
Protocol. Conversely, you can't filter on the color filter fields with a
_ws.col.Custom field, but you can filter on frame.coloring_rule.name
directly, so that doesn't matter.

Remove the special handling for the -e option to tshark. Note that
the behavior is a little different now, because fixed field names
are used instead of the titles (using the titles allowed illegal
filter names, because it wasn't going through the filter engine.)
For default names, this means that they're no longer capitalized,
so "_ws.col.info" instead of "_ws.col.Info" - hopefully a small
price in exchange for the filters working everywhere.

They're also set before the postdissectors, so postdissectors can
have access.

Anything that depends on whether a packet and previous packets are
displayed (COL_DELTA_TIME_DIS or COL_CUMULATIVE_BYTES) doesn't work
the way most people expect, so don't register fields for those.
(The same is already true of color filters that use those, along with
color filters that use the color filter fields.)

Fix #16576. Fix #17971. Fix #4684. Fix #13491. Fix #13941.

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 109cd48a - epan: Register static column fields and make them filterable
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10522/diffs?diff_id=674486082&start_sha=361200705a79e84cc3c2c4dfc5b1ec7023dbf51e)
I'm not sure if we have a use case for COL_CUSTOM? Adding a column with "_ws.col.custom" will add all values from custom columns into one, but it looks a bit messy.

I am not sure that it makes sense to allow creating a column with these fields instead of using them for filtering and output. It gets into some of the same recursive issues as color filters that depend on the color filter fields.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10522/diffs?diff_id=677800598&start_sha=6a3d146fbb4fa823731ac5a89ad24afb99a82d55#415f71799b1c4cace257230be3f90bd54499e5b8_2418_2424)
I removed processing the custom columns. It can always been added later if there's a use case.
In my build `pinfo->cinfo` is not set yet.

It is only set when the columns are constructed, which can slow down dissection by a factor of 2 from doing the string operations on the columns. There's a bunch of checks that should set it whenever columns are needed - I get it to exist whenever there's a display filter, read filter, tap filter, or `-e` option to tshark. What are you trying?

Possibly I missed a case? Maybe something with a color filter?

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10522/diffs?diff_id=679691756&start_sha=1b052b352878bcce7358443e8efcbea24299a74b)
What do we expect "_ws.col.expert" to show? I get nothing from this.

It has the text entries, but like all the columns, it only works if you have a column of that type in your configuration. It will fill it in if the column exists but is hidden, but not if the column isn't in the prefs at all.

That extends from not just filtering to if you create a column with the field "_ws.col.expert" it doesn't get filled in unless you have a column of the builtin expert type. Without a COL_EXPERT entry in the prefs, the proper part of the cinfo struct isn't created, so the data isn't there to fill in later.

That's why I've toyed with deregistering the column fields with the prefs change, because that is confusing. Or perhaps these fields should just not be allowed for custom columns, only for filtering. Or the entire "how to create the columns" should be changed.
The _ws.col fields are not that useful for assigning to custom columns (I guess maybe in a multi field column.)

-selected. Column names may be used prefixed with "_ws.col."

-// === Removed Features and Support
+* The text of any configured column (displayed or hidden) can be filtered
+anywhere that filters are used - in display filters, filters in taps, coloring
+rules, Wireshark read filters, and the -Y, -R, and -e options to tshark,
+the "Apply as Filter" GUI option, etc.
+** The filter field names are prefixed by "_ws.col", followed by a lowercase
+version of the COL_ name found in epan/column-utils.h, e.g. "_ws.col.info"

+because the columns must be constructed, so when the same filtering
+can be achieved via other fields, prefer that.

+* With the addition of the universal and consistent filtering support for
+column text, the previous support in the -e option to tshark for displaying

+The previous implementation allowed names that are not legal filter names
+and wsbuglink:16576[silently ignored columns that didn't exist.]
